scope.description: Whole apachearrow application/library breadth across useful functional families.
scope.denominator: Typed arrays and tables, CSV/columnar interchange, datasets, compute, streaming and cross-language memory exchange.

coverage.rationale: Prepared tables can now publish an explicitly opted-in typed CSV alongside Parquet and the report, connecting selected rows to declared CSV consumers. This deepens bounded interchange; general datasets, streaming, memory exchange and most compute remain absent, so whole-application breadth stays at 10%.

scope.description: Explicit typed nullable CSV table selection, renaming, widening and null replacement into independently checked Parquet and optional typed CSV publications.
scope.denominator: User intent and domain decisions within the named supported workflows, including declared inputs, composition and useful outputs; excluded application features do not enter this score.

abstraction.rationale: Declared schemas, predicates and publication intent hide native parsing, table operations and writer configuration. Users still choose physical types and compatible downstream contracts; the existing 75% estimate is retained within this bounded interchange family.

limitations: Six flat scalar types and bounded CSV input; no general Parquet ingestion, nested types, metadata, units or dataset operations.

Optional CSV preserves the closed lexical/null contract but carries no schema. Consumers must declare compatible types; a literal nonnull reserved null token cannot be represented. Spreadsheet consumers may support a stricter subset.
Canonical floating-point text is an observed PyArrow 26.0.0 writer contract; sample probes and independent typed readback support this bounded implementation, not every future native writer.
Subjective source-contract assessment, not an exhaustive API measurement. Verification confidence, native availability and source-bound qualification remain independent of both strength scores.
